ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $CD$ is the median to the hypotenuse $AB$. A line through point A perpendicular to $CD$ intersects $CD$ and $CB$ at points E and F, respectively. If $\tan B = \frac{2}{3}$, what is the value of $\frac{AE}{EF}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and CD is the median to the hypotenuse AB,\\
$\therefore$ CD=BD, $\angle ACD+\angle BCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BCD=\angle B$,\\
$\therefore$ $\tan\angle B=\tan\angle BCD=\frac{EF}{CE}=\frac{2}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ let EF=2x, CE=3x,\\
$\because$ AE$\perp$CD,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEC=\angle CEF=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAF+\angle ACD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAF=\angle BCD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AEC\sim \triangle CEF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{CE}=\frac{CE}{EF}$,\\
$\therefore$ AE=$\frac{CE^2}{EF}=\frac{9}{2}x$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EF}=\frac{\frac{9}{2}x}{2x}=\boxed{\frac{9}{4}}$.

method.method_draft: Use analytic geometry with coordinates. From the image, read the configuration as a right triangle with C at the lower-left corner, A vertically above C, B horizontally to the right of C, D on hypotenuse AB, CD drawn, and AF crossing CD at E and the base CB at F. From the text, tan B = AC/BC = 2/3, so choose convenient coordinates C = (0,0), B = (3,0), and A = (0,2). Since CD is the median to hypotenuse AB, D is the midpoint of A and B, so D = (3/2,1). The slope of CD is 1/(3/2) = 2/3, so the line through A perpendicular to CD has slope -3/2 and equation y = 2 - (3/2)x. Its intersection with CB, where y = 0, is F = (4/3,0). Its intersection with CD, whose equation is y = (2/3)x, is E; solve (2/3)x = 2 - (3/2)x to get x = 12/13 and y = 8/13. Since A, E, and F are collinear, AE/EF equals the ratio of their horizontal coordinate differences along the same line: AE/EF = (12/13 - 0)/(4/3 - 12/13) = 9/4.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个直角三角形 ABC，C 在左下角，A 在左上方，B 在右下方；AC 竖直，CB 水平，AB 是斜边。点 D 在斜边 AB 上，线段 CD 从 C 连到 D。另有一条从 A 出发的直线向下经过 CD 上的 E，再交 CB 于 F；题目说明这条直线垂直于 CD。推理：采用坐标法。因为 tan B = AC/BC = 2/3，可取 C=(0,0), B=(3,0), A=(0,2)。CD 是斜边 AB 的中线，所以 D 是 AB 的中点，即 D=(3/2,1)。因此 CD 的斜率为 1/(3/2)=2/3。过 A 且垂直于 CD 的直线斜率为 -3/2，方程为 y=2-(3/2)x。它与 CB，即 y=0，相交于 F，得 0=2-(3/2)x，所以 F=(4/3,0)。CD 的方程为 y=(2/3)x。求 E：令 (2/3)x=2-(3/2)x，得 (13/6)x=2，所以 x=12/13，y=8/13，即 E=(12/13,8/13)。因为 A、E、F 共线，所以 AE/EF 等于同一直线上对应水平坐标差之比：AE/EF = (12/13-0)/(4/3-12/13) = (12/13)/(16/39) = 9/4。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $CD$ is the median to the hypotenuse $AB$. A line through point A perpendicular to $CD$ intersects $CD$ and $CB$ at points E and F, respectively. If $\tan B = \frac{2}{3}$, what is the value of $\frac{AE}{EF}$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $CD$ is the median to the hypotenuse $AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $CD=BD$, $\angle ACD+\angle BCD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BCD=\angle B$,\\
$\therefore$ $\tan\angle B=\tan\angle BCD=\frac{EF}{CE}=\frac{2}{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ let $EF=2x$, $CE=3x$,\\
$\because$ $AE\perp CD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEC=\angle CEF=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAF+\angle ACD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAF=\angle BCD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AEC\sim \triangle CEF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{CE}=\frac{CE}{EF}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AE=\frac{CE^2}{EF}=\frac{9}{2}x$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AE}{EF}=\frac{\frac{9}{2}x}{2x}=\boxed{\frac{9}{4}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is at the upper left, C is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, AC is vertical, CB is horizontal, so AB is the hypotenuse. D is located on the hypotenuse AB, and CD connects from C to D. There is also an oblique line starting from A that passes through E on CD, and then intersects CB at F. Reasoning: Because triangle ABC is right-angled at C, and CD is the median on the hypotenuse AB, D is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, so CD = BD. Thus triangle BCD is an isosceles triangle, giving angle BCD = angle CBD = angle B. It is known that tan B = 2/3, so tan angle BCD = 2/3. In right triangle CEF, CE is on CD, EF is on the line passing through A and perpendicular to CD, therefore angle CEF = 90°, and tan angle BCD = EF/CE = 2/3. Let EF = 2x, CE = 3x. Also because AE is perpendicular to CD, triangle AEC is also a right triangle. From AC perpendicular to CB and AE perpendicular to CD, angle CAF and angle BCD are equal, therefore triangle AEC and triangle CEF are similar. The corresponding sides satisfy AE/CE = CE/EF, so AE = CE^2/EF = (3x)^2/(2x) = 9x/2. Thus AE/EF = (9x/2)/(2x) = 9/4.
